name: British top-boost style (EL84 pair, no feedback)
notes: 60s British 'chime' style: bright, jangly, breaks up early and sweetly, very touch-sensitive. Its key features: EL84 power tubes, a tube rectifier (lots of sag), and NO global feedback loop (so there is no feedback block). Path: V1 -> volume -> top boost stage -> treble/bass circuit -> phase inverter with a 'cut' control -> 2x EL84. FROM SCHEMATICS (fairly sure): EL84 pair, no global negative feedback, tube rectifier, a cut control after the phase inverter, 12AX7 preamp stages. UNSURE / APPROXIMATED: the top boost treble/bass circuit is a different circuit from the tone stack block and is approximated here with EQ bands (a real block for it is still to be added); all bias values; the cut control as a 6 kHz low-pass; phase inverter as one triode that gets half the input (each triode of the real long-tailed pair sees half the signal, so it has twice the headroom of a single stage); EL84 pair at 320 V into 8k with -13 V bias (a real one is cathode biased).
